# Bencium

> Design-first AI advisory helping organisations understand, train for and implement
> agentic AI without giving up human judgement, evidence or control. Bencium combines
> training, consulting and hands-on implementation across multi-agent workflows,
> regulated healthcare, publishing and specialist knowledge systems. Based in London
> and working globally, with production systems, open-source tools and peer-reviewed
> research available through the Projects archive.

## About

- [About Bencium](https://bencium.io/about/): Founder background, credentials, mission
- [FAQ](https://bencium.io/faq/): 15 questions covering engagement models, team prep, success metrics, compliance

## Evidence & Projects

- [Projects](https://bencium.io/projects/): Production systems, open-source tools and AI research
- MedHubAI: Regulated healthcare AI deployed across 10 clinics and recognised among the EIT Finalists
- Anna: Peer-reviewed oncology support AI, indexed by PubMed as PMID 41819064
- brandguide/AI: Used by 700+ people and available as a Skill through a standard supported by 40+ AI development tools
- Bencium Skill Marketplace: Open-source agent skills with 400+ GitHub stars and support across 40+ AI tools
- mameds Medication Information: Winning EU-funded collaboration with Greek and Spanish partners

## Dictionary

- [The Agent Orchestration Dictionary](https://bencium.io/workshops/#dictionary): 87 AI, LLM and machine-learning terms explained in plain English for knowledge workers who want to run fleets of AI agents, not build them. Every term has its own page with a diagram and schema.org DefinedTerm markup. Also published in Hungarian at https://bencium.io/hu/workshops/#dictionary
  - 1. The raw material (15 terms): what a model actually is, and what it eats
  - 2. Talking to a model well (8 terms): getting good answers on purpose, not by luck
  - 3. Getting facts right (17 terms): hallucination, grounding, RAG, evals — the part that decides whether AI is usable for regulated work
  - 4. Giving an agent hands (12 terms): tools, function calling, MCP, skills, loops
  - 5. Orchestrating many agents (22 terms): one agent is an assistant, many are a workforce
  - 6. Keeping it running in the real world (13 terms): cost, latency, observability, prompt injection
